data.title: Google Willow Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in Paradoxical Game
data.description:
Google’s Willow quantum processor is demonstrating one of quantum mechanics’ deepest features by winning a game rooted in an impossible mathematical paradox.

The superconducting chip says researchers achieved a 98.3% win rate in the magic square game across 100,000 trials per version, exceeding the classical limit of 88.89%.

Researchers ran the game using shared entanglement on the processor, where qubits coordinate answers without a pre-written table of fixed values.

Shashwat Kumar and Rodrigo Cortiñas explain the results in detail.

“Our qubits win the magic square game 98.3% of the time, exceed the classical limit on a contextuality test, and outperform classical strategies in tasks spanning up to 105 qubits.”

The team also measured a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality value of 5.590, well above the classical bound of 4.

They add context on the measurement’s significance.

“We measured ? = 5.590 ± 0.008. Comfortably past the classical bound of 4 and only 7% away from the quantum limit.”

The effect held in scaled tests including a GHZ parity game with up to 71 qubits and tasks spanning 105 qubits, while verifying genuine entanglement across 45 qubits.

These benchmarks proved sensitive at catching subtle hardware errors that other tests miss, positioning contextuality as a deeper resource than entanglement for certain quantum advantages.

The findings appeared November 19, 2026, in Science.

data.title: Police Warn Scammers Posing as Banks and Financial Regulator on WhatsApp, Sending Couriers To Collect Victims’ Cards
data.description:
Police say scammers posing as banks and the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority are using WhatsApp to trick people into handing their bank cards to couriers.

Authorities say fraudsters have been using WhatsApp messages, voice calls and video calls to pose as a trusted authority after a spike in reports, reports the BBC.

The callers claim the person’s bank account has been compromised or that their money has to be moved to a safe account.

Fraud protect officer Dale Richardson of the force’s economic and cyber crime unit says the scammers have displayed the FCA logo or a bank’s logo to look genuine.

“This makes the scam feel more real and convincing, so it’s really important people are aware of this tactic and that they encourage friends and family to be vigilant.”

Some victims have also been asked to share their phone screen, which can let the fraudsters see sensitive information or get into online banking.

Richardson says the calls are the first step in courier fraud, where the victim is tricked into handing over bank cards, PINs, cash or valuables to a courier sent to their home.

“In some of the reports we’ve seen in Nottinghamshire, Uber taxis have been used as the courier and bank cards and PINs collected.

The courier has then used these in stores, including Apple, to purchase goods.”

Some victims have lost hundreds of pounds.

Richardson says the FCA, banks and police will never ask for personal information or for money to be transferred.

He asks people to be alert to unprompted contact and to never hand over sensitive information such as PINs and passwords.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Releases Patches for Vulnerability Allowing Attackers to Stall Nodes
data.description:
Bitcoin Core is releasing patches to address a vulnerability that allows attackers to stall nodes by repeatedly announcing the same orphan transaction identifier up to 50,000 times in a single message.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, stems from how the software has handled orphan transactions since version 29.0.

When a peer announces an orphan via its wtxid, Bitcoin Core builds a list of missing parents and checks them without skipping duplicates in inv messages.

An attacker could first send an orphan with thousands of missing parents and then repeat its wtxid 50,000 times.

The disclosure explains the impact in detail.

“A peer could stop a node from processing blocks and transactions temporarily by repeatedly announcing an orphan transaction with many missing parents.”

Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks.

A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and duplicate entries were not skipped.

The issue affects versions 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4, and 31.0 through 31.2, with the 29.x series having reached end of life.

The fix processes each announced transaction only once and was merged into master in August 2026 before backports in November.

Bitcoin Core says the vulnerability was discovered through an automated LLM scan in Project Loupe at Spiral and independently reported by another researcher.

“This issue was discovered through an automated LLM scan, as part of Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral.”

Updated releases 30.5 and 31.3 arrived on November 20.

data.title: Coinbase Eyes In-House US Prediction Markets by Mid-2027 After CFTC Clearinghouse Approval
data.description:
Coinbase is preparing to launch its own prediction markets directly in the United States by the first half of 2027.

The company currently offers these event contracts through a partnership with Kalshi but says it plans to bring the offering in-house to gain greater control over product listings and capture more trading revenue.

Both retail and institutional customers are expected to have access once the service goes live.

This development is supported by recent regulatory progress including CFTC approval of Coinbase Clearing LLC as the first USDC-native derivatives clearing organization.

The approval completes Coinbase’s full stack of CFTC-regulated infrastructure including a futures commission merchant and designated contract market.

It enables direct creation and settlement of fully collateralized contracts with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement.

“Today’s CFTC approval completes Coinbase’s end-to-end derivatives infrastructure enabling us to bring more regulated derivatives products to market with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement.”

The company noted it will continue using partners for certain products such as margined derivatives and upcoming single stock perps.

The target timeline for the in-house launch is the first half of 2027.

data.title: Senate Approves Bill Banning Prediction Market Bets on War, Terrorism and Death
data.description:
The U.S. Senate has approved legislation barring prediction markets from offering contracts tied to some of the most sensitive events.

The measure known as the Discouraging Exploitative Assassination, Tragedy, and Harm Betting in Event Trading Systems Act or DEATH BETS Act amends the Commodity Exchange Act to stop registered entities from listing or clearing such contracts.

It specifically prohibits agreements referencing terrorism, assassination, war, U.S. Armed Forces military operations, or similar activities.

The bill also bans contracts expected to resolve principally based on an individual’s death.

Senator Adam Schiff is highlighting the passage alongside Senator John Curtis.

“BREAKING: The Senate just passed my bill with @SenJohnCurtis to prohibit prediction markets from listing contracts involving terrorism, assassination, war, military operations, or an individual’s death. With this bill, Congress is making it clear that these bets should be illegal.”

The legislation includes a rule of construction preserving other permitted activities under existing law.

It was introduced on March 10, 2026, and passed the Senate with an amendment by voice vote on November 19, 2026.

The action targets event contracts on prediction platforms while leaving other trading unaffected.

data.title: Florida Man Accused of 32 Fraudulent Wire Transfers Worth More Than $600,000
data.description:
A 22-year-old Miami man is accused of making 32 fraudulent wire transfers worth more than $600,000.

Donnell Collier Jr. allegedly carried out an account-takeover scheme tied to a nationwide bank fraud crackdown, according to federal court records, reports CBS12.

Collier faces charges of wire fraud conspiracy, wire fraud and bank fraud.

If convicted, he could face up to 80 years in federal prison.

His arrest was one of five in Florida tied to fraud schemes linked to more than $54 million in losses at over 65 financial institutions nationwide.

The operation involved FBI offices in Miami, Nashville, New York, Columbia, Houston and Omaha.

Four suspects were arrested in South Florida while a fifth South Florida resident was arrested in Central Florida.

Brioden Jean and Derek Val Pierre-Paul are charged in Tennessee with wire fraud conspiracy and two counts of wire fraud.

Kevin Lopez and John Sardinas are charged in Iowa with money laundering conspiracy and four counts of money laundering.

data.title: Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets
data.description:
A U.S. appellate court is affirming Maryland’s authority to enforce its sports wagering laws against the prediction market platform Kalshi.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit says the Commodity Exchange Act does not clearly preempt the state’s gaming laws even for event contracts on a CFTC-regulated designated contract market.

Judge Gregory concurring emphasizes that the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power.

“Because the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power, I would not infer that Congress displaced Maryland’s concurrent authority absent a clear expression of its intent to do so.”

The decision rejects Kalshi’s preemption arguments and finds no impossibility or obstacle to federal objectives.

Maryland Attorney General Anthony G. Brown says the ruling requires Kalshi to meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.

“When betting platforms operate outside State oversight, Marylanders lose the protections that keep gambling fair and safe.”

“Today’s ruling means Kalshi must meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.”

The per curiam opinion in case No. 25-1892 was decided November 18, 2026, after arguments on May 7, 2026.

data.title: DBS Teams Up With Circle to Give Asian Institutions 24/7 USDC Minting and Redemption
data.description:
A major Asian bank is partnering with a leading stablecoin issuer to give institutions direct round-the-clock access to minting and redeeming USDC.

DBS says the partnership expands institutional access to the stablecoin across Asia by enabling eligible clients to mint and redeem it through the bank.

The arrangement enables 24/7 USD-USDC settlement for seamless movement of value between fiat and digital environments.

Both firms are also participating in the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Project BLOOM initiative to promote interoperability among tokenised money forms.

A DBS survey of 422 business leaders from firms with over USD 500 million in revenue across 11 markets found that 88% are already deploying or piloting tokenised money use cases.

Stablecoins lead adoption at 63%, followed by tokenised deposits and money market funds.

Over 60% of respondents are adopting or planning to adopt stablecoins, with expectations for benefits like improved auditability (72%) and real-time cross-border payments (71%).

Institutions are increasingly looking to tokenised money to manage liquidity more efficiently and support their growth across new markets.

“This partnership meets that demand by bringing together Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure and global reach with DBS’ trusted banking, liquidity and digital asset capabilities in Asia.”

Financial institutions are increasingly looking for trusted ways to access stablecoins and integrate blockchain-based infrastructure into their financial operations.

“By combining Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure with DBS’ institutional banking and liquidity capabilities, our partnership represents an important step in expanding institutional access to USDC across Asia, while strengthening the banking infrastructure supporting its global adoption.”

data.title: Florida Man Sentenced in North Carolina to 51 Months for $800,000 Cell Phone Tower Fraud Scheme
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have secured a 51-month prison sentence against a Florida man who ran a fraudulent cell phone tower consulting scheme that collected more than $800,000 from hundreds of victims.

Alexander Francise Blasscyk, 48, of Windermere, Florida, was sentenced in federal court in Charlotte, North Carolina, to 51 months in prison plus three years of supervised release and ordered to pay $1,039,115.30 in restitution, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of North Carolina.

According to court documents, Blasscyk defrauded victims by falsely claiming to be a cell tower consultant. Between 2018 and 2024, he told individuals, including residents of Ashe County, that he would market their properties to cell tower companies and wireless carriers for a fee. He also promised to negotiate lease agreements that would allow the companies to build towers on their land in exchange for rental payments.

Hundreds of victims, including individuals and businesses, paid Blasscyk or companies he controlled more than $800,000 for the purported consulting services and related expenses. However, little to no work was performed. Blasscyk did not market the properties to wireless carriers or cell tower companies as promised, nor did he negotiate the lease agreements he had offered to secure.

To persuade victims to hand over their money, Blasscyk provided false and fraudulent documents through his company.

Blasscyk used two companies to solicit fees for nonexistent work marketing land for tower leases and instead spent the money on personal expenses, including hotels, short-term rentals, restaurants and bars.

U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson said the defendant gave people the hope of passive income.

“Blasscyk gave people the hope of passive income — making false promises to lease land to cell phone tower companies while collecting consulting fees. But Blasscyk did no consulting, made no such deals, and created fake documents to cover up his fraud.”

He pleaded guilty to wire fraud in October 2025.

data.title: Investment Scams Cost Americans $27,500,000 in Eight Months, Topping Online Purchase Fraud
data.description:
Investment scams have cost Americans $27.5 million in reported losses over eight months, more than any other fraud type that commonly targets older adults.

Homewatch CareGivers says it analyzed Better Business Bureau Scam Tracker reports from January 1st to August 24th.

Online purchase fraud was the most reported scam, with 53,934 reports and $25 million in losses.

Phishing was second by volume, with 27,389 reports and $9 million in losses.

Investment scams ranked lower in volume, with 1,110 reports. Even so, their losses were the highest of any category in the study at $27.5 million.

“Although Online Purchase fraud and Phishing are the most commonly reported scams targeting seniors, Investment scams cost Americans more money. The Better Business Bureau tracked 1,110 Investment scams in our data period, and there were 15 types of scams that were more prevalent than this. But because of the high figures involved in investment scams, the total reported loss equals $27.5 million — three times the cost of Phishing to scam victims and dozens of times the cost of most other fraud types.”

Las Vegas had the highest rate of scams that commonly target seniors among 25 major cities, at 97 per 100,000 residents over an eight-month period.

Victims in Houston lost $1,009,000 to investment fraud, representing 9% of the total losses in the fraud category in Texas.

New Hampshire had the highest rate among states, with 816 reports, or 58 per 100,000 residents.

The figures include reports from victims of all ages, not just seniors.
